stories.headline: Lecornu announces €710M fuel aid package as Middle East war drives prolonged energy crisis
stories.summary: Prime Minister Lecornu held his first press conference at Matignon on 21 May, unveiling €710M in targeted fuel subsidies for workers, taxi drivers, fishing fleets, and home-care workers, citing the ongoing US-Israel-Iran war and Strait of Hormuz blockade. He refused a broad tax cut on fuel, warned the conflict 'will last,' and said the total fiscal cost — already €6B+ — will require new budget cuts to be identified by mid-June.

stories.headline: RN internal tensions over 2027 programme: Le Pen and Bardella diverge on pension reform age
stories.summary: Le Pen and Bardella gave contradictory signals on the RN's flagship promise to lower retirement age to 62: Bardella told German press the question was 'being examined,' while Le Pen publicly maintained the 62-year commitment. Multiple outlets reported this as symptomatic of a broader strategic fracture between a social-populist camp loyal to Le Pen and a more business-oriented current around Bardella, with the July 7 appeal verdict on Le Pen's eligibility adding urgency.

stories.headline: Macron names ally Emmanuel Moulin as Banque de France governor, drawing opposition from across parties
stories.summary: Parliament validated the nomination of Emmanuel Moulin — former Élysée Secretary-General and Macron confidant — as governor of the Banque de France on 20 May, despite over 54% of parliamentarians voting against him (3/5 threshold required for veto). The appointment triggered a broader controversy about Macron systematically installing loyalists (also including Richard Ferrand at the Conseil Constitutionnel, Amélie de Montchalin at the Cour des Comptes, and Macron's speechwriter Baptiste Rossi at France Télévisions) in key state positions ahead of the 2027 election.

stories.headline: Bardella's girlfriend at centre of media storm: Bourbon des Deux-Siciles family sues Belgian outlet for defamation
stories.summary: Following Jordan Bardella's public disclosure of his relationship with aristocrat Maria Carolina de Bourbon des Deux-Siciles (via Paris Match cover in April), media scrutiny intensified over her family's ties to a $600M inheritance dispute linked to her grandfather's alleged corruption. The family filed a defamation suit against Belgian outlet DHnet. Bardella's own preliminary presidential campaign was cited as the underlying target.

stories.headline: Macron condemns Russian Oreshnik missile strike on Ukraine and calls Lukashenko in diplomatic outreach
stories.summary: Following an overnight Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv using the Oreshnik hypersonic missile on 23–24 May, President Macron condemned the strike as a 'headlong rush' and called Belarusian president Lukashenko — the first such call since 2022 — urging Minsk not to be drawn into Russia's 'war of aggression.' EU foreign policy chief Kallas also condemned the attack.

stories.headline: France bans Israeli minister Ben-Gvir over Gaza flotilla detainee taunts
stories.summary: Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot announced on 23–24 May that France has banned Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir from entry after footage emerged of him taunting bound Gaza flotilla activists detained by Israeli forces. France simultaneously summoned the Israeli ambassador and was among several countries — including Italy, the Netherlands, and Canada — taking diplomatic action.

stories.headline: Macron slavery reparations ceremony: supports Code Noir repeal, opens debate on reparations
stories.summary: At a ceremony marking the 25th anniversary of the Loi Taubira recognising the slave trade as a crime against humanity, Macron on 21 May supported parliament's bill to symbolically repeal the Code Noir and for the first time evoked the 'immense question' of reparations — without making concrete commitments. He also announced a joint Franco-Ghanaian scientific commission on the subject.

stories.headline: Gabriel Attal officially declares 2027 presidential candidacy, inherits Macron's 2022 social media accounts
stories.summary: Former Prime Minister Gabriel Attal formally declared his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election on 22 May at a citizen debate in Mur-de-Barrez (Aveyron). It also emerged that Attal had taken over and rebranded Macron's 2022 campaign social media accounts (some 85,000 followers) to 'Attal président,' causing friction with Renaissance and provoking criticism from Marine Le Pen.
